claims.head: The Maple Leafs give up shots, and the Avalanche take them
claims.call: The Avalanche’s shot volume score is at least their usual 124.
claims.see: About 57 shot attempts at 5-on-5, usually around 32 shots on goal on the scoreboard.
claims.body: The Avalanche love to shoot, and the Maple Leafs keep letting teams do it. Get ready for a shooting gallery.
claims.nums: Colorado 1st for shot volume (score 124) · Toronto 28th for shot suppression

claims.head: Shots should fly both ways
claims.call: The game’s pace score is above 109, faster than either team’s usual.
claims.see: More than 72 shots between them at 5-on-5, on goal or wide, which usually means 58 or more shots on goal on the scoreboard.
claims.body: The Maple Leafs play some of the league’s fastest games, and so do the Avalanche. We think this one runs hotter than either team’s usual.

claims.head: The Avalanche kill penalties far better than the Maple Leafs
claims.body: On the penalty kill, Colorado is one of the league’s best, but Toronto is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Penalties should hurt the Maple Leafs more than the Avalanche.

COL.head: A big edge for the Avalanche
COL.body: Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Maple Leafs’ best way in is keeping dangerous shots away.

TOR.head: A steep climb for the Maple Leafs
TOR.body: Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. To pull this off, the Maple Leafs can start with keeping dangerous shots away, plus a goalie who steals the show.
